subject: phy
title: Kinematics
subtitle: Displacement, velocity, acceleration and equations of motion.
concept: Displacement, velocity and acceleration are vector quantities; distance and speed are scalars.
The five kinematic equations (SUVAT) apply to uniform (constant) acceleration only.
Graphs of motion: gradient of displacement–time = velocity; gradient of velocity–time = acceleration; area under v–t graph = displacement.

notes.heading: Definitions
items: Displacement (s): change in position; vector (direction matters).
Velocity (v): rate of change of displacement; v = Δs/Δt; vector.
Acceleration (a): rate of change of velocity; a = Δv/Δt; vector.
Speed and distance are scalar equivalents (magnitude only).

notes.heading: SUVAT Equations
items: Valid only for uniform (constant) acceleration; use g = 9.81 m s⁻² (or 10 m s⁻² if specified) for free fall.

notes.heading: Motion Graphs
items: s–t graph: gradient = instantaneous velocity; straight line = constant velocity; curve = acceleration.
v–t graph: gradient = acceleration; area under curve = displacement; horizontal line = constant velocity.
a–t graph: area under curve = change in velocity.
Free fall: parabolic s–t curve; straight v–t line with gradient g downward.

notes.heading: Projectile Motion
items: Two independent components: horizontal (constant velocity, no acceleration) and vertical (constant acceleration = g downward).
Horizontal: x = v_x t. Vertical: use SUVAT with a = g = 9.81 m s⁻².
Time of flight determined from vertical component; range from horizontal × time.

definitions.body: The vector quantity representing change in position; has magnitude and direction.
Acceleration that is constant in both magnitude and direction; required for SUVAT equations to apply.
An object moving under gravity only; has constant horizontal velocity and constant downward acceleration g.

workedExamples.q: A ball is thrown horizontally at 15 m s⁻¹ from a cliff 45 m high. Find the time of flight and horizontal range. (g = 10 m s⁻²)

steps.text: s = ut + ½at²; 45 = 0 + ½×10×t²; t² = 9; t = 3.0 s

mistakes: Applying SUVAT to non-uniform acceleration (e.g. air resistance present — use graphs instead).
Forgetting that at maximum height, the vertical velocity is zero (not horizontal).
Mixing up which direction is positive — always define positive direction first.
tips: In projectile problems: resolve into horizontal (a=0) and vertical (a=g) components; treat them independently.
The gradient of a curved s–t graph at a point = instantaneous velocity (draw tangent at that point).
Free fall: g acts downward; if upward is positive, a = −9.81 m s⁻².

flashcards.q: What are the five SUVAT equations?
What does the area under a v–t graph represent?
flashcards.a: Displacement (the area between the line and the time axis).

flashcards.q: What is the velocity of a projectile at its highest point?
flashcards.a: The vertical component is zero; the horizontal component remains constant (equal to initial horizontal velocity).

flashcards.q: What is the gradient of a displacement–time graph?
flashcards.a: Velocity (instantaneous velocity at a point = gradient of tangent to the curve).

flashcards.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m s⁻¹ in 4 s. What is its acceleration?
What condition must hold for SUVAT equations to be valid?
flashcards.a: Acceleration must be uniform (constant in magnitude and direction).

questions.q: A stone falls from rest. How far has it fallen after 3.0 s? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
What does the gradient of a v–t graph represent?
questions.exp: Gradient of v–t graph = Δv/Δt = acceleration.

questions.q: A projectile is launched horizontally. Which statement is correct?
opts: Horizontal velocity increases due to g
Horizontal and vertical motions are independent
questions.exp: Horizontal and vertical motions are independent; horizontal velocity is constant (no horizontal force); vertical velocity increases due to g.
On an s–t graph, constant acceleration gives a parabolic (curved) shape; on a v–t graph it gives a straight (non-horizontal) line.

questions.q: v² = u² + 2as. A car with u = 0, a = 3 m s⁻², s = 24 m. Find v.

recall: Describe what each graph feature represents in s–t and v–t graphs.
Solve a projectile problem by resolving into horizontal and vertical components.
Distinguish between scalar and vector quantities.
Calculate displacement from a v–t graph.
